name: Global temperature
summary: Global temperature 2.01°C above pre-industrial on 2 Nov, a record for the date
state: ERA5 data for 2 Nov put global surface air temperature at 14.92°C, about 2.01°C above pre-industrial levels, a record for the calendar date and above the 1.6°C Alert line (Climate Reanalyzer). The estimate adds 0.88°C to the 1991–2020 anomaly of 1.13°C. Readings for the most recent eight days ranged from about 1.74°C to 2.02°C.
for_you: A single day's reading is not the same as long-term warming passing a limit, but sustained high readings raise the odds of heat, drought and marine heat stress around the world.
rubric_hit: Alert: +2.01°C > +1.6°C line, and a record high for the calendar date (2 Nov)

sources.title: Climate Reanalyzer — ERA5 daily global surface air temperature

why: Global temperature is the master climate variable; each tenth of a degree raises extreme-weather risk.
drivers: Greenhouse gases, El Niño/La Niña, aerosols, solar cycle.

rubric.alert: > +1.6°C, or a record high for the calendar date.
rubric.normal: Daily global anomaly < +1.3°C above pre-industrial (ERA5 vs 1991–2020 + 0.88°C).
